record.name: Notion
record.one_liner: Notion provides a REST API, OAuth 2.0 public connections, internal static tokens, and personal access tokens to automate and build integrations for pages, databases, and workspace content.

auth.notes: Notion supports multiple token-based mechanisms including static API tokens for internal connections, personal access tokens (PATs), and OAuth 2.0 for public connections.

access.notes: Developers can sign up for a Notion account and create internal connections, public connections, or personal access tokens directly via the Developer portal.

api_surface.notes: The public API follows RESTful conventions, supports webhooks for real-time events, and offers an official JavaScript SDK alongside cURL examples.

buildability.reasoning: Self-serve credentials are straightforward to obtain from the Developer portal (such as personal access tokens or internal connection tokens), and the REST API is thoroughly documented with a JavaScript SDK and cURL examples.

evidence.claim: Notion supports internal connections, public connections, and personal access tokens powered by a REST API.
The Notion API follows RESTful conventions and requests are sent to https://api.notion.com with request/response bodies encoded as JSON.
Webhooks allow connections to receive real-time updates via secure HTTP POST requests for page and database changes.
